service.description: The groups, each with its kind (registered: a capability bundle; custom: a group of a registered purpose an access administrator created; other), app, purpose, current member and permission counts, its app gates (artifact groups), and the markers that explain a refusal before it happens: privileged (in the effective privileged-group list) and the sealed permissions it grants (from the effective sealed-permission list). Narrowed by text (id or description, ignoring case), app, kind (registered, custom, other or supported), a permission it grants now and privilegedOnly. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

One group: its profile and markers, its memberships (current, future and ended, each with its revision), its permission grants (sealed and registered marked), its artifact bindings with their filter sets, its preferences and the registered preference keys, its grant revision (what preview#Grants and apply#Grants compare), and whether the actor may change it and why not; with includeOptions the registered bundles a grant may come from. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

A custom group of a registered purpose (a UserGroupType with optionIndicator Y), with no members or grants: never privileged (a privileged or reserved id is refused) and never an existing id. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

parameter.name: userGroupId
parameter.description: 3 to 60 capital letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter

service.description: A group's safe profile (description; a custom group's purpose) and sign-in policy (requireAuthcFactor, ipAllowed, comma separated patterns as login reads them), for a registered bundle, a custom group or a privileged group the actor is a member of; refused when stale (expectedRevision, the group's lastUpdatedStamp as get#Group gives it) or when the policy would leave no administration path. The factor and IP flags are audit-logged with the reason. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

A dated membership of a user in a registered bundle or a custom group, from fromDate (now when empty) to thruDate; with the fromDate of an existing membership and its revision, a change of its end date. Refused for an unregistered group (UNREGISTERED_BUNDLE), a bundle whose delegable permission the actor lacks, a privileged group the actor is not in (PRIVILEGED_GROUP, before the EECA would refuse it), an overlapping membership, a stale revision or a change that would leave no administration path. The dates are audit-logged with the reason; ended memberships are kept. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

Ends a membership at thruDate (now when empty), keeping the row, in any group: a privileged group's only by a member, and never the last administration path. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE and the membership's revision.

The effective change of a grant request on a group, nothing written: each permission or artifact binding added or ended, before and after, the kind and bundle it comes from, whether the actor may make it and why not (UNREGISTERED_GRANT, SEALED_PERMISSION, a group refusal), the current members it reaches, and the grant revision apply#Grants expects. A row rule (a filter set bound to a registered binding) is allowed only when a registered bundle the actor may assign names the set for that artifact group (UNREGISTERED_SCOPE), the group has a binding of the registered type or the request adds it (SCOPE_UNBOUND) that carries no filter set of its own (SCOPE_CONFIGURED), and it is added: removing one widens what members read and stays Tools' (SCOPE_REMOVAL). Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

parameter.name: grantList
parameter.description: Each a Map: action add or end, and userPermissionId, artifactGroupId or bundleGroupId alone (each of the bundle's permissions and bindings); bundleGroupId beside a permission or artifact group names the bundle it comes from; fromDate and thruDate optional. With entityFilterSetId beside artifactGroupId, a row rule: the filter set bound to the group's registered binding on that artifact group (add only)

service.description: The previewed grant change: dated UserGroupPermission rows added or ended (never deleted) and registered artifact bindings added (ArtifactAuthz with the bundle's filter sets) or removed (recorded in the audit log), and registered row rules bound (an ArtifactAuthzFilter on each of the group's bindings of the registered type, recorded in the audit log); refused as a whole when any part is refused or the grants or their filter sets changed since the preview (expectedRevision). Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

parameter.name: grantList
parameter.description: Each a Map: action add or end, and userPermissionId, artifactGroupId or bundleGroupId alone (each of the bundle's permissions and bindings); bundleGroupId beside a permission or artifact group names the bundle it comes from; fromDate and thruDate optional. With entityFilterSetId beside artifactGroupId, a row rule: the filter set bound to the group's registered binding on that artifact group (add only)

service.description: A group's default for a registered preference key (a UserPreferenceKey Enumeration; its optionValue types the value: indicator, boolean, number or text), with its priority; an empty value removes the default. For a group the actor may change, with the existing row's revision. Audit-logged with the reason. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

A grant proposal (impl-admin §4, F11): the registered bundles an app supplies for an account it provisions, each allowed or refused with its reason by the delegation rules of store#Membership for the actor (registered only, its delegable permission, a privileged group only by a member, no sealed grant carried to a non-holder); nothing written. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW or ADMIN_IDENTITY_VIEW.

The memberships of a grant proposal for one account (a staff account Mantle creates, later an accepted invitation), each a dated row from fromDate (now when empty) written with authorization on, so the sealed and privileged EECAs decide it; refused whole, nothing written, when any bundle is refused (check#GrantProposal); a bundle the account is already in is left. The dates are audit-logged with the reason. The framework knows no organization: the caller scopes the account. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE or ADMIN_IDENTITY_MANAGE.

The capability matrix over the registry: the registered capabilities of an app (all apps when none) as rows, each a launcher binding or a permission by its kind (launcher, view, edit, export, sensitive; one row each, so a launcher is never read as a view or a change, nor a change as a view), against at most 8 groups (the app's first 6 registered bundles when none are named; moreGroupCount the rest). Each cell says what the group holds now (granted, scheduled, none, or advanced: another rule on the artifact group, never changed here), a launcher's bound filter sets and whether a registered one is missing, whether the actor may grant or end it and the reason when not, and the change proposed for it (proposedList). cellList is the same cells one per row, the matrix's list. What a group holds that no registered bundle describes is in unsupportedList, read only. Nothing is written or evaluated: the framework's permissions and artifact authorizations decide access, and preview#Grants and apply#Grants each change. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

parameter.name: kind
parameter.description: launcher, view, edit, export or sensitive

parameter.name: proposedList
parameter.description: Each a Map: userGroupId, action add or end, and userPermissionId or artifactGroupId; marks the cell, nothing more

service.description: The row rules in effect: each EntityFilterSet bound to a group's artifact binding (ArtifactAuthzFilter), with the entities it filters, whether a condition applies it, and its source (registered: the group's own bundle registers it; bundle: another registered bundle does, as a grant copies it; configuration: deployed configuration or Tools). A registered binding lacking a filter set its bundle registers (and carrying none of its own) is listed as missing, with whether the actor may bind it through apply#Grants and the group's grant revision. A page (pageIndex from 0, pageSize up to 200) narrowed by group, artifact group, filter set, state (bound, missing), source and text; filterSetList is every filter set. A filter's expression and apply condition are never returned, and nothing is written: arbitrary filters, removing one and raw entity rules stay Tools'. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

The access and grant review of up to 60 groups (those named, or an app's registered bundles) as of a date and time (now when empty), one projection for print and CSV: each group's permission grants open then (kind, dates, the scope its services still check), its app gates (as they are now: an artifact binding has no dates) with their filter sets, and its members then. Sealed permissions are left out and counted (sealedOmitted per group); allowed IPs, preference values and filter expressions are never in it. The framework knows no organization: a caller that scopes members filters memberList. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.

The Capabilities screen's context over get#Capabilities: the group columns, the matrix rows (a capability with a cell per group) and the list rows (the same cells, one a row), each cell with its state text, its bound row rules, the proposal made for it and the proposal its control would make next (changes with its token added or withdrawn); what the groups hold that no registered bundle describes; the find form's options; and, when changes are proposed, their effect on each group from preview#Grants, whether all may be applied and the grant revisions to apply them at. changes is the proposal the screen carries: comma separated tokens group~a|e~p:permission or group~a|e~a:artifactGroup, at most 40. More than 8 groups or 40 changes is answered as failure, the reason, with nothing else but the proposal as given. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW; nothing is written.

parameter.name: groups
parameter.description: Group ids, comma separated or a list; at most 8

service.description: Applies a matrix proposal (changes, as get#MatrixContext) group by group through apply#Grants: each group's changes as one change at the grant revision previewed for it (revisions, a JSON object by group), in its own transaction. A group that is refused (a stale revision, a sealed permission, a privileged group, an unregistered grant, the administration path) or fails is named with its reason and the others still apply; remainingChanges are the tokens not applied. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_MANAGE.

The lockout preview of a group's sign-in rules (design-admin §6 GroupSignInRules), nothing written: for the factor requirement and allowed addresses proposed, how many current members the group has, how many of them have no confirmed factor (who could not finish a sign-in once a factor is required), whether the actor's own address is admitted by the proposed addresses, and whether the change keeps an administration path (allowed, else ADMINISTRATION_PATH with the reason, or the group refusal store#Group would give); counts only, no member is named. Needs ADMIN_ACCESS_VIEW.
